summary: Stealth GPU throttling causing sustained throughput degradation in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC, NimbleDocs reported persistent degradation in inference throughput and elevated request timeouts on their Dedicated pool in us-west. The degradation presents as elevated p95/p99 token latencies and an increase in 504s when running production traffic patterns (short chat-style requests). Impact: Customer reports 30-50% drop in throughput and downstream application timeouts affecting user facing search autocomplete features. This is a dedicated, reserved pool for NimbleDocs; no configuration changes were made on their side. Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved), pool-id: ded-nimble-usw-11, GPU type A100-40G, cluster autoscaling enabled with min=2 max=8 nodes, workload consists of small batched chat (<64 tokens) and embedding requests.

Observed behavior: Latency regressed gradually over ~30 minutes, not a hard outage. Telemetry shows a correlation between GPU utilization oscillations and host-level 'cuda_context_switch' spikes. Metrics suggest contention on GPU SMs with low overall GPU memory pressure. Hypothesis is noisy co-located processes or an OS-level kernel preemption causing sustained scheduling latency on some nodes, combined with autoscaler not reacting quickly due to conservative surge thresholds.

Customer impact and business context: NimbleDocs is enterprise-tier and using Dedicated for SLA predictability; incident affects search SLA and there's active support escalation (account manager notified).
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool matching ded-nimble-usw-11 (A100-40G, k8s node pool config identical)
Deploy rwdx-7b-v2 model server with continuous small chat workload at 1200 rps sustained
Observe p95/p99 token latency and 504 rate over 30-60 minutes while autoscaler is set to conservative thresholds (scale step 1, cool-down 5m)
Run host-level synthetic GPU microbenchmarks concurrently on a subset of nodes to emulate background noisy work and watch for scheduling/context-switch spikes
investigation_notes: Initial triage: No recent deploys for customer; control-plane healthy; IAM and network not implicated.
Telemetry: GPU SM utilization oscillates with periods of low throughput despite high kernel scheduling delay. Memory usage stays moderate, ruling out OOM-based eviction.
Node inspection: node-04 and node-07 show high 'nvidia-smi' driver reported context-switch counters and elevated 'iowait' system CPU; dmesg shows occasional 'GPU reset' warnings (low frequency).

Autoscaler: scaling policy prevented additional nodes because pod CPU requests were within target but GPU-level contention not surfaced to autoscaler metrics. Autoscaler thresholds are CPU/memory-based, not GPU-scheduled-wait-aware.
Hypothesis 1: Non-Redwood background process (customer or infra job) on shared underlying instance consuming GPU SM time leading to unfair scheduling (noisy neighbor).
Hypothesis 2: Kernel-level preemption bug in specific GPU driver version causing long contexts; correlated driver version on affected nodes is 510.xx. Still investigating earlier upgrades.
Hypothesis 3: Autoscaler mis-sizing — node pool min of 2 is insufficient for bursty GPU-saturated workloads and conservative cooldown prevented rapid scale-out.
Reproduction attempts: Running microbenchmarks on a control node reproduced p95 increase when microbenchmarks were active, indicating susceptibility to co-located GPU activity.
Customer data: NimbleDocs confirms no batch-training scheduled; they provided access logs and request patterns which match production behavior.
Support actions: Temporarily routed 30% of traffic to fallback pool in another az which restored latency to baseline; observed throughput recovery after reroute.
comments: Ava Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Received report from customer at 03:20 UTC. Opened ticket and started telemetry capture. Notified SRE channel #support and #sre.
Jordan Reyes (NimbleDocs, customer) 2026-03-10: Confirmed no customer-side changes. Provided request logs and allowed temporary traffic reroute for mitigation.
Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10: Identified node-04/07 anomalies. Spun up diagnostic pods to collect nvidia-smi and strace traces. Suggested temporary traffic split and node isolation.

Priya Singh (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11: Observed driver 510.73.x on affected hosts; filing internal ticket to check CVEs/regressions. Proposed short-term scheduler change to prefer fenced nodes for Dedicated pools.
Ava Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted traffic reroute mitigation; currently monitoring. Planning post-incident RCA and follow-up with account team.
resolution_summary: Mitigation: 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC we shifted 30% of NimbleDocs traffic to a cold fallback dedicated pool in eu-west and then to a same-region isolated pool after additional nodes were provisioned. This reduced p95 to baseline. Root cause likely combination of noisy co-located GPU activity and autoscaler not surfacing GPU scheduling delays. Temporary fixes: isolated affected nodes (cordon & drain), increased dedicated pool min nodes from 2 to 3 for NimbleDocs, and added a telemetry alert for 'cuda_context_switch' spikes. Engineering to validate driver version and push a scheduler patch that enforces exclusive GPU allocation for Dedicated pools.
follow_up_actions: ENG-Task: Validate driver 510.73.x and test kernel upgrades on canary nodes (owner: Priya Singh)
SCHED-Change: Implement GPU scheduling isolation flag for dedicated pools to prevent co-location (owner: Marcus Chen)
AUTOSCALE-Change: Extend autoscaler to include a GPU_wait_metric and reduce cooldown for dedicated pools (owner: Platform Team)
POSTMORTEM: Complete RCA document and customer-facing summary within 5 business days (owner: Support)
Billing: Review potential SLA credit for NimbleDocs (owner: Account Ops)
Monitoring: Add runbook step and dashboard tile for context-switch telemetry and integrate into alerting
